newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 25.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
INVESTIGATING AGENCY AGAINST TABLING OF BOFORS PAPERS

The Central Bureau of Investigations (CBI) objected to the proposal for tabling the papers related to the Bofors' gun scandal in parliament. It said the move would jeopardise investigation in several cases being pursued abroad. The CBI reportedly told the Prime Minister's office that such a step may lead the Swiss authorities to hold back the second set of documents, expected to arrive here in the coming months.
The Economic Times
FORMER FINANCE MINISTER AGAINST MINIMUM TAX

Former finance minister Manmohan Singh expressed reservations about continuing with the minimum alternate tax (MAT). In a pre-Budget interview, he suggested correcting distortions in the tax system at source rather than giving incentives with one hand and taking them away with the other. He said zero-tax companies existed because of liberal depreciation norms and export incentives.
BHARTI TELENET PAYS LICENCE FEE

Bharati Telenet submitted the first instalment of license fee for operating basic telecommunication services in the Madhya Pradesh circle. Bharti was the first company out of 12 letter of intent holders for basic services to submit the licence fee within the stipulated period.
PROTESTS FORCE APEX BANK TO AMEND ORDINANCE

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) proposed certain necessary changes in the provisions of an ordinance to prevent unincorporated bodies from accepting deposits for lending onward. The RBI clarified the recent amendment was not intended to prevent individuals from accepting deposits from other individuals for business purposes. The changes became necessary following the scare it created among partnership firms and trade bodies.
LEFT PARTIES PRESS FOR FUNDING STATE-OWNED FIRMS

The Left parties were pressurising the government to allocate significant funds for state-owned firms (PSUs) in the forthcoming budget. Buoyoed by its success in getting the ruling coalition to announce a new Targeted Public Distribution System, the Left was preparing its case on revival of sick PSUs. The sectors of particular concern for the Left were fertilisers, jute, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and some heavy industries.
Financial Express
PIRAMAL TO TAP MARKET WITH $ 60.5 MLN OFFER

Nicholas Piramal India would tap the Euro convertible bond market with an offering aggregating $60.5 million. The offer, which was likely to be made in the first quarter of 1997/98 (April-March), would part-finance the group's 2.75 billion rupee expansion plans. The offer would carry an average interest rate of Libor plus 90 basis points.
TOP GLOBAL BANKS VIE FOR ADVISORY SERVICES

Global investment banks were pitching hard for financial advisory services in the power and telecommunication sectors. This was despite infrastructure projects being caught up with domestic regulatory bodies and environmental issues. Banks in the fray included Deutsch Morgan Grenfell, SC Warburg, BZW, ANZ Investment Bank, BankAm, Toronto Dominon, Union Bank of Switzerland, ABN Amro and Chase Investment.
ICICI TO FLOAT GLOBAL MEDIUM-TERM NOTE

Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (ICICI) would become the first Indian financial institution to float a global medium-term note. The Finance Ministry has cleared ICICI's plan to raise $500 million through the programme. ICICI proposed to launch the programme with an inaugural issue of subordinated floating rate note (FRN) aggregating $100 million in the first week of March.
Business Standard
74 PCT GOVERNMENT SELLOFF TO REVIVE 11 FIRMS

The Industry Ministry decided to offload up to 74 percent of government stake in 11 state-owned firms (PSUs) as a last-ditch effort to turn around these sick units. The ministry also proposed a two billion rupee revolving fund, consisting of 10 percent of the disinvestment proceeds, for quick implementation of turnaround plans.
COMPANY BOARDS MAY GET MORE POWERS

The expert panel for recasting the Companies Act proposed delegation of additional powers to the boards of companies for approving annual and half-yearly accounts, mergers and acquisitions and raising money abroad, subject to clearance by shareholders. The panel also proposed to clip the powers of individual directors and managing directors regarding loans taken by them from their firms by capping the eligibility criterion at five times the annual pay package of each of these professionals.
NEW FOOD SUBSIDY TO RAISE BILL BY 24 BLN RUPEES

The food subsidy bill will increase by 24 billion rupees in the coming year with the implementation of the new targeted public distribution system (TPDS). The TPDS was aimed at giving wheat and rice to the poor at specially reduced prices and charging marginally higher prices from those living above the poverty bracket. The decision about these prices was taken after deliberations within the ruling United Front coalition and subsequently approved by the cabinet.
21 FIRMS BID FOR FIRST TRANSMISSION JOINT VENTURE

Twenty-one companies were in the fray to partner the Karnataka power utility (KEB) in the first-ever joint venture for power transmission from independent power units. The firms vying to become KEB's partner in the eight billion rupee project include National Grid Company Plc, Hyundai and Rolls Royce. The bid document was sold for 50,000 rupees alongwith a 1.5 million rupee non-refundable fee.
BOURSE INDEX SHEDS 81 POINTS AS BUDGET NEARS

Pre-budget nervousness pulled down stock prices on the Bombay bourse (BSE). The BSE sensitive index (Sensex) registered a loss of 81.02 points at 3358.47. The loss was attributed to sustained bull unloading coupled with lack of fresh buying on the first day of the new account. Operators and institutional buyers appeared cautious after the Sensex breached the psychological 3400 point barrier.
Business Line
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS SEEK BETTER OFFER TERMS

Financial institutions (FIs) indicated to the Polysindo group of Indonesia to better their offer for taking over the ailing Vijay Mallya group company, Best and Crompton. The Indonesian company sought several concessions including a partial write-off of the principal amount which the company owed to FIs and banks, as part of the rehabilitation package. The lenders were opposed to the string of conditions attached by the Polysindo group, especially the part waiver of the principal amount.
